name: Ringo Corponation Hollow Channel Communicator
description:
The Hollow Channel Communicator is a bone-conduction audio device that forgoes all radio transmission in favor of direct physical vibration, transmitting voice communication through contact with any rigid surface — a table, a wall, a vehicle chassis, a railing — that is shared between sender and receiver. Both parties press a small adhesive transducer pad against the same connected physical structure; the sender's voice is converted to vibration, travels through the material, and is reconstructed into audio at the receiver's end. Because the signal never enters the electromagnetic spectrum, it is entirely invisible to radio frequency monitoring, spectrum analysis, and signal intelligence equipment of any kind. There is no transmission to intercept, no frequency to identify, and no encryption to break — because the communication exists only as mechanical vibration within a physical object.

The device's limitations are significant and define its use cases precisely. Both communicating parties must be in contact with the same continuous rigid structure simultaneously, which in practice means the Hollow Channel is used for short-range coordination in confined environments — shared buildings, adjacent rooms, connected vehicles, underground infrastructure. The audio fidelity is acceptable rather than excellent, with some frequency loss through dense or acoustically absorptive materials, and the system cannot carry data, only voice. Ringo Corponation designed the transducer pads to be thin enough to adhere under clothing or inside a jacket lining, making them concealable during covert use.

The Hollow Channel Communicator occupies a niche that other communication tools cannot fill: environments where any electromagnetic emission, however small or encrypted, will trigger automated security responses. High-security corporate vaults, certain government facilities, and the most sensitive private residences in GLMZ are swept continuously for RF activity, making conventional comms suicidal for anyone operating covertly inside them. In these environments, the Hollow Channel is not merely useful — it is the only viable option for maintaining contact between team members.

specifications.dimensions: Transducer pad: 3.2cm x 2.1cm x 0.3cm; Processing unit: 4.1cm x 2.8cm x 0.9cm
specifications.transmission_medium: Any continuous rigid surface (metal, concrete, glass, composite)
specifications.effective_range: Up to 60m through steel; 20–35m through reinforced concrete; variable through composites
specifications.audio_quality: 70–85% voice clarity depending on surface material and path length
specifications.user_capacity: Up to 6 paired units on a single surface connection

tactical_use: In practice, teams using the Hollow Channel Communicator pre-identify shared structural elements in target environments during planning — the steel frame of a building, a shared ventilation duct, a continuous concrete floor — and assign each team member to a contact point along that structure. During operations inside RF-monitored environments, the system allows coordinated action without triggering any electronic countermeasure. The primary operational limitation is that team members must maintain physical contact with the shared surface, which constrains movement. Experienced operators compensate by using the system only for critical coordination moments, maintaining contact briefly to transmit and then moving freely between transmissions. The device is also used for near-silent communication in surveillance scenarios where even whispered speech carries risk.
cultural_context: The Hollow Channel Communicator is unrestricted in GLMZ partly because its use cases are narrow enough that it does not register as a threat to the communications monitoring infrastructure that the city's corporate and municipal authorities depend on. It cannot be used to coordinate large groups across distances, it cannot carry data, and it requires physical proximity to a shared structure. What it can do — allow two or three people in the same building to communicate without any detectable signal — is treated as insufficiently dangerous to regulate. This legal status makes it the only professional-grade covert communication tool that can be openly purchased, which in turn has made it a favorite of corporate security consultants who need to demonstrate to clients that their RF-swept facilities can still support internal coordination.
known_users: Infiltration specialists operating in RF-monitored facilities
Paranoid private citizens in high-security residences
story_hooks: A building's structural survey reveals that the Hollow Channel has been used to transmit through its frame for months — the transducer pad adhesive residue marks a path that traces a route through the building no authorized personnel should have been taking.

A Ringo Corponation product recall notice goes out for a specific batch of Hollow Channel Communicators, citing 'unintended acoustic resonance behavior' — recipients who investigate discover that the affected units are transmitting a faint secondary signal at a frequency consistent with a surveillance carrier wave.

Two opposing teams inside the same target building independently discover they are both using the Hollow Channel on the same structural element, and can hear each other's transmissions — turning a covert operation into an improvised negotiation.

A murder is committed inside an RF-swept facility with no conventional communications traffic recorded during the relevant window — but forensic analysis of the building's structural steel reveals vibration patterns consistent with Hollow Channel use in the minutes before the victim died.
